@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1A8MDQ9NTZX4A0N8JZBA4XN
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8280'
+title: 'Real-model test: update(items:) makes new ids selectable and removed ids unreachable'
+---
+## What
+
+The second real-model test. It covers the seam FoundationModelsRanker's own suite cannot reach: this package's `update(items:)` rebuilding the selection tier over this package's `MetadataIndex`, then a real model selecting from the rebuilt catalog.
+
+File to create:
+- `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryIntegrationTests/HotReloadRealModelTests.swift`
+
+Shape:
+1. Build a `MetadataSearcher` in `.selection` mode over a starting catalog, wired to a real `LanguageModelSession` exactly as in `^xmt6fmc`.
+2. Call `await searcher.update(items:)` with a catalog that **adds** one clearly distinct item and **removes** one.
+3. Search with an intent that only the added item can answer. Assert the added id is returned.
+4. Search with an intent that only the removed item could have answered. Assert the removed id is never returned, and that no `.unknownSelectedId` fires for it.
+
+`update(items:)` is at `Sources/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistry/MetadataSearcher.swift:346`; `search(intent:limit:)` at `:410`.
+
+### Why this one is ours and not FoundationModelsRanker's
+
+Ranker's four real-model tests drive its own `Searcher` facade and its own `.selectionDefault` preamble. None of them calls `update(items:)`, because Ranker's facade has no hot reload — its own doc comment says the catalog is fixed for the lifetime of the facade. The rebuild path is this package's, over this package's `MetadataIndex` conformance to `SelectionCatalog`, with this package's `.librarianDefault` preamble.
+
+That combination — our catalog conformance feeding Ranker's `assemblePrefix` — is exactly where the `## <id>` defect lived, and Ranker found it, not us. This test puts a real model on that seam.
+
+### Make the added and removed items unmistakable
+
+The assertion is about catalog membership, not model taste. Choose an added item whose block shares no vocabulary with the rest of the catalog, so an on-topic intent has exactly one defensible answer. Same for the removed one. A test that depends on the model preferring one plausible item over another plausible item is a flaky test, not a hot-reload test.
+
+### Scope
+
+Under-budget path only. Do not assert embed catch-up or cosine behavior: this package ships no real embedder, and FoundationModels exposes no embedding API at all — a search for `embedding` over the SDK's `FoundationModels.swiftinterface` returns zero hits.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] The test calls `await searcher.update(items:)` on a live searcher, not a freshly constructed one.
+- [ ] An intent answerable only by the added item returns that id.
+- [ ] An intent that the removed item would have answered never returns the removed id.
+- [ ] No `.unknownSelectedId` diagnostic fires for the removed id.
+- [ ] The test calls `ModelAvailability.requireAvailable()` first.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `IntegrationTests/Tests/.../HotReloadRealModelTests.swift` — one test covering add, one covering remove; or one test asserting both, if it stays under the sizing limit.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests`. Both assertions hold.
+- [ ] Run it three times and record the pass rate in a comment on this card.
+- [ ] Prove the remove half can fail: temporarily skip the `update(items:)` call so the removed item is still in the catalog, confirm the test fails, revert.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
